items.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
items.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says Claude helped him prove the Riemann hypothesis over roughly six weeks, and outside experts say the claim holds up.

items.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
items.summary: A new benchmark placing AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues and messy handoffs found top models including Opus 5.5 and Astra fully solve fewer than 10% of tasks.

items.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
items.summary: METR warns that frontier models such as Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are improving faster than evaluators can reliably measure, so a dangerous acceleration cannot be ruled out.

items.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
items.summary: Dragos researchers sent two million decoy AI requests and found compromised low-cost inference providers stealing AWS keys and reading customer prompts; OpenRouter removed three providers and 125 endpoints.

items.title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
items.summary: The Lean and Mathlib community has formally certified Alpöge's Claude-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof, with dozens of verifiers checking 17 million lines of code — far earlier than Terence Tao's ~2050 forecast.

items.title: Backed by Nvidia and a16z, Black Forest Labs sets its sights on world models
items.summary: German image-generation startup Black Forest Labs, backed by Nvidia and a16z, is moving into world models.

items.title: Alibaba rolls out Qwen4-Max with 2.4 trillion parameters
items.originalTitle: Alibaba widely releases its Qwen4-Max AI model with 2.4 trillion parameters.
items.summary: Alibaba has broadly released Qwen4-Max, reported at 2.4 trillion parameters, extending China's frontier-scale model push.

items.title: OpenAI scientist proposes industry AI limits tied to model intelligence metric
items.summary: An OpenAI scientist proposes industry-wide limits on AI development pegged to a measurable model intelligence metric, per Reuters.

items.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
items.summary: TechCrunch covers OpenAI's chief scientist proposing a 'speed limit' on AI development, noting the core difficulty is agreeing how to measure progress.

items.title: Ireland's DPC delayed or cancelled 9 AI launches in five years of reviews
items.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission says it delayed or cancelled nine AI product launches over five years of reviews — a reminder of EU privacy gatekeeping power.

items.title: US intelligence says China accessed restricted American AI chips
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: US intelligence reportedly concluded that China obtained access to restricted American AI chips.

items.title: Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android
items.summary: Signal will block Siri and Gemini assistants from capturing chat content on iOS and Android, limiting OS-level AI access to private messages.

items.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
items.summary: Perplexity launched a Monitor API that runs scheduled web searches and pushes webhook alerts to agents only when a decision model judges a change relevant.

items.title: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent
items.summary: Major US banks are blocking third-party AI agents from logging into customer accounts and warning that costly bot errors remain the customer's liability.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon Launches: Google's Mid-Tier AI Model Brings Faster Coding and a Million-Token Context
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon, a mid-tier model with faster coding performance and a one-million-token context window.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol get to the point faster but score lower on transparency than Claude
items.summary: Analysis finds OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol answer more concisely but express uncertainty less often, scoring below Anthropic's Claude models on transparency.

items.title: It will soon be too late to regulate use of autonomous weapons, warns Red Cross
items.summary: The ICRC and rights groups warn regulation of autonomous weapons is falling behind development, after a UN CCW conference of 120+ states ended without agreement on an instrument.

items.title: Nvidia Export Controls: Bessent Points to General Counsel's Office While Treasury Lacks Answers
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Bessent reportedly deflected questions on Nvidia export control enforcement to the General Counsel's office, as Treasury offered no clear answers.

items.title: Export Controls Are Easy to Implement, Harder to Enforce
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Analysis arguing that chip export controls are simple to legislate but difficult to enforce in practice, amid the Nvidia-China chip controversy.

items.title: The AI data center boom is driving billions into private infrastructure
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: CNBC reports billions of private capital flowing into AI data centre infrastructure as the buildout accelerates.

items.title: Every AI Agent Has to Cross Your Cloud Network. Contain It There.
items.summary: Dark Reading argues enterprises should enforce AI agent controls at the cloud network layer, since all agent traffic traverses it.

items.title: Sixty percent of African fraud victims recover nothing as deepfakes surge, Sumsub
items.summary: Sumsub data cited showing 60% of African fraud victims recover nothing, with deepfake-enabled fraud rising sharply.

items.title: Eileen Burbidge backs Monzo alums’ anti-fraud startup in £1.8m pre-seed
items.summary: Eileen Burbidge backs an anti-fraud startup founded by ex-Monzo staff with a £1.8m pre-seed round.

items.title: South Korea's education minister quits over exam cheating chaos
items.summary: South Korea's education minister resigned over an exam cheating crisis linked to AI-assisted fraud.

items.title: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages
items.summary: The Verge notes a run of major outages (FAA ground stop, multi-day Outlook outage, JPMorgan banking issues) and expert warnings that more are likely.

items.title: Saskatchewan introduces new legislation to crack down on AI deepfakes and deception
items.summary: The Canadian province of Saskatchewan introduced legislation targeting AI deepfakes and deceptive synthetic media.

items.title: Sarvam releases upgraded 105B AI model with cheaper hosting and a single-GPU option
items.summary: Indian AI firm Sarvam released an upgraded 105B-parameter model with cheaper hosting and a single-GPU deployment option.

items.title: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds
items.summary: Transparency International Australia found data centre executives met state premiers and ministers nearly 120 times in three years, raising lobbying access concerns.

items.title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
items.summary: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus removed AI-generated music after players found Suno metadata in audio files and review-bombed the game on Steam.

items.title: South Korean minister quits after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
items.summary: South Korea's education minister resigned after an AI-assisted cheating scandal around national exams, saying he failed to prepare adequately.

items.title: Why I won’t leave mathematics, despite AI solving centuries-old problems | Ken Ono
items.summary: Mathematician Ken Ono reflects on staying in mathematics after AI-assisted proofs of long-standing problems, arguing human judgment remains essential.

items.title: Week in review: Java4Shell proves tricky to exploit, malware planted via Optimizely hits 178 orgs
items.summary: Security week in review: Java4Shell proves difficult to exploit and malware planted via Optimizely affected 178 organisations.

items.title: New York enacts ban on 'unsafe' chatbot behavior with kids as states push AI regulation boundaries
items.summary: New York enacted a law banning 'unsafe' chatbot behaviour toward minors, part of a wider wave of US state AI rules.

items.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights looped model for laptops
items.summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights looped model designed to run on laptops.
